title: Characterization of venous return and perfusion of the lower extremities during anesthesia for a DaVinci surgery in steep Trendelenburg position
summary:
During anesthesia in general, and specifically during robot-assisted removal of the prostate in a steep head-down tilt (Trendelenburg position), a multitude of cardiovascular changes occur, for which there is currently insufficient data.
The project described here aims to investigate, on the one hand, the function of the veins and, on the other hand, the blood perfusion of the legs.
Veins represent the blood reservoir of the body, and the question is how anesthesia, surgery, and/or a steep positioning affect venous function. Furthermore, robot-assisted surgeries in a steep head-down tilt position cause a shift of blood volume towards the heart, thereby increasing the pressures in the veins preceding the heart. However, the extent to which blood perfusion of the legs is impaired in the head-down tilt position is also insufficiently investigated.
Therefore, this observational study aims to examine cardiovascular function before, during, and after surgery for robot-assisted removal of the prostate, with respect to venous function and lower extremity perfusion in the head-down tilt position. This could identify potential starting points for future therapy optimizations.

interventions.name: Patients undergoing elective robot-assisted radical prostatectomy in steep Trendelenburg position.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients undergoing an elective robot-assisted radical prostatectomy in the steep Trendelenburg position at the Evangelischen Kliniken Essen-Mitte
Exclusion criteria:
The presence and/or treatment of: Age < 18 years, Missing written informed consent, Insufficient language comprehension, Unwillingness to have pseudonymized disease data stored locally and to share anonymized data within the scope of the clinical study, ASA status higher than III, Heart failure, defined by dyspnea greater than or equal to NYHA III, Ischemic heart disease, defined by Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) Angina Class II or higher, Severe myocardial valvular stenosis or insufficiency, Chronic renal failure requiring hemodialysis, Pulmonary hypertension requiring oxygen therapy and/or pharmacological treatment
